la Salut — Barcelona, Spain

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

La Salut's specific press coverage centres on the Turó de la Rovira/Búnkers del Carmel viewpoint on its edge (shared with el Carmel), a popular sunset/tourist spot: Metròpoli Obert (Jul 2023) reported car break-ins and a 76-year-old resident beaten and robbed of his phone confronting tourists trying to enter the fenced-off bunkers at night, plus unauthorized late-night drinking gatherings that led the city to fence and close the area after 7:30pm. Daytime visits show no comparable incident reports. Sources checked: Metròpoli Obert, 15 Jul 2023.

Frequently asked questions

Is la Salut safe?

Wandroz currently rates la Salut in Barcelona, Spain as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is la Salut safe at night?

At night, la Salut is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

la Salut's day rating (relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
